Here's an interesting possibility shaping up that may well be the best case scenario for all involved.

First of all, the Rams are the one true Los Angeles football team. They belong there and the owner appears fully ready to move them there. He has the best stadium location and the team that has the best chance of building a legacy and fanbase in LA. The Rams should be in LA.

Second, the Chargers and San Diego are not getting along, in fact it looks like a total break-up. Everyone hates the owners, and the owner hates the stadium plan offered and hopes to get a "downtown" football stadium, which is ridiculous and never going to happen. Considering their delivery of mostly mediocrity, the fans are rapidly getting fed-up with the Chargers. Threatening to move to LA, of all places, has been the final straw. This is a fanbase ready to say goodbye.

The owner, meanwhile, just wants a fancy new taxpayer-funded stadium. California isn't the place to get that, so enter St. Louis - the city that appears willing to completely fuck itself over financially if need be to house football. Life in St Louis is apparently miserable enough to worship sports in this way and it sounds like a match made in heaven for the Chargers. The sting of the Rams moving home will be greatly cleared up by the relocation of the Chargers to St. Louis. It also helps the NFL, who definitely do not want to let a paid stadium go to waste. The pieces are in place to see this happen.

Third, the fucking Raiders. The Raiders are getting nothing from Oakland and deserve nothing. The fans have seem them leave before, rechristening them "The Traders," and are resigned to it happening again. They don't care, they can still be Raider fans without 8 home games. ESPECIALLY if the team moves to San Diego. LA is a stab-in-the-back for Bay Area fans, but honestly San Diego would be ok. Additionally, the Raiders have a deep Mexican-American fanbase that could be greatly enhanced in San Diego, where they could really become california's team after having played in Oakland, LA, and San Diego over two decades. The fanbase they'd be pursuing would be different than the La Jolla north-county crowd that has failed to keep the Chargers. The San Diego Raiders would be another beast, and for marketing and other purposes this is a great move. Further, the existing stadium in San Diego actually represents an upgrade for the Raiders! They can comfortably play there while working out the details of their new park without all of the demands and baggage the current Chargers owners bring to the table.

Finally, Oakland wins. Fans can still like the Raiders, or they can keep liking the 49ers, who have carried a huge amount of the Bay Area fanbase after winning all those Super Bowls while the Raiders were in Los Angeles. Even better, this actually goes a long way towards solving the A's problem, due to conflicts in the stadium siting with the Raiders. Baseball, with 81 home games, represents a far better investment for the city than football. If the Raiders dispatch to San Diego the fans won't be too mad, because they're a short flight away in familiar territory, and the A's can take over the Oakland market completely.

I think this is a great scenario for the NFL and the teams and cities involved. Nobody really loses a team here.
